00011| Welcome to the Next.js documentation!
00012| 
00013| ## What is Next.js?
00014| 
00015| Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.
00016| 
00017| It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.
00018| 
00019| Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
00020| 
00021| ## How to use the docs
00022| 
00023| The docs are organized into 3 sections:
00024| 
00025| - [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
00026| - [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
00027| - [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
00028| 
00029| Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
00030| 
00031| ## App Router and Pages Router
00032| 
00033| Next.js has two different routers:
00034| 
00035| - **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
00036| - **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
00037| 
00038| At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
00039| 
00040| ### React version handling
00041| 
00042| The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
00043| 
00044| - **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
00045| 
00046| - **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
00047| 
00048| This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
00049| 
00050| ## Pre-requisite knowledge
00051| 
00052| Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
00053| 
00054| - HTML
00055| - CSS
00056| - JavaScript
00057| - React
00058| 
00059| If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
00060| 
00061| ## Accessibility
00062| 
00063| For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
00064| 
00065| ## Join our Community
00066| 
00067| If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).
00068|

</file>

00219|           env: process.env,
00220|           encoding: 'utf8',
00221|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00222|         });
00223|         if ((exportRes.status == null ? -1 : exportRes.status) === 0) {
00224|           observedModel = extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportRes.stdout || '');
00225|         }
00226|       } catch {
00227|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00228|       }
00229|     }
00230|   }
00231|   const observedModelOrNull = observedModel ?? null;
00232| 
00233|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00234|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00235|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');

00238|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;

00240|       ok: false,
00241|       output,
00242|       transcript,
00243|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00244|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00245|       agentExitCode,
00246|     };
00247|   }
00248| 
00249|   return {
00250|     ok: true,
00251|     output,
00252|     transcript,
00253|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00254|     error: null,
00255|     agentExitCode,
00256|   };
00257| }
00258| 
00259| /* ───────────────────────��─── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00260| 
00261| // True when this file is executed directly (`node run.mjs ...`), false when imported.
00262| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];

00264| if (isMain) {

00269|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00270|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00271|   let result;

00273|     result = await runAgent(input);
00274|   } catch (e) {
00275|     result = {
00276|       ok: false,
00277|       output: '',
00278|       transcript: null,
00279|       observedModel: null,
00280|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00281|       agentExitCode: -1,
00282|     };
00283|   }
00284|

00286|   try {

00289|   } catch {

00291|   }
00292|

00294|   process.stdout.write(
00295|     '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
00296|       JSON.stringify({
00297|         ok: result.ok,
00298|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00299|         error: result.error,
00300|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00301|       }) +
00302|       '\n'
00303|   );
00304| 
00305|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00306|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).
00307|   process.exit(0);
00308| }

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

title: How to upgrade to version 16

description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use an AI agent (recommended)

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

Give the agent this prompt:

```prompt
Upgrade this app to Next.js 16.

Before editing code, make sure AGENTS.md points at version-matched Next.js docs. If it is missing or outdated, follow [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs), then read AGENTS.md.

Then follow the [Next.js 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16) as the source of truth for the migration. Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#using-the-codemod) when you're ready to run the mechanical upgrade.

title: Linking and Navigating
description: Learn how the built-in navigation optimizations work, including prefetching, prerendering, and client-side navigation, and how to optimize navigation for dynamic routes and slow networks.
related:
  links:
    - app/api-reference/components/link
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading
    - app/guides/prefetching
---

In Next.js, routes are rendered on the server by default. This often means the client has to wait for a server response before a new route can be shown. Next.js comes with built-in [prefetching](#prefetching), [streaming](#streaming), and [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) ensuring navigation stays fast and responsive.

This guide explains how navigation works in Next.js and how you can optimize it for [dynamic routes](#dynamic-routes-without-loadingtsx) and [slow networks](#slow-networks).

## How navigation works

To understand how navigation works in Next.js, it helps to be familiar with the following concepts:

- [Server Rendering](#server-rendering)
- [Prefetching](#prefetching)

title: Linking and Navigating
description: Learn how the built-in navigation optimizations work, including prefetching, prerendering, and client-side navigation, and how to optimize navigation for dynamic routes and slow networks.

In Next.js, routes are rendered on the server by default. This often means the client has to wait for a server response before a new route can be shown. Next.js comes with built-in [prefetching](#prefetching), [streaming](#streaming), and [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) ensuring navigation stays fast and responsive.

This guide explains how navigation works in Next.js and how you can optimize it for [dynamic routes](#dynamic-routes-without-loadingtsx) and [slow networks](#slow-networks).

## How navigation works

To understand how navigation works in Next.js, it helps to be familiar with the following concepts:

- [Server Rendering](#server-rendering)
- [Prefetching](#prefetching)

events.content:
Migration complete and verified against the Next.js 16 docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`.

**What changed:**
- `app/layout.tsx` — root layout (`<html lang="en">`/`<body>`) + shared `metadata` (favicon icon, default title/description). Replaces `_app.tsx` + `_document.tsx`.
- `app/page.tsx` — home page; `next/head` → inherited metadata, internal `<a>` → `next/link` `<Link>`.
- `app/about/page.tsx` — about page; page-specific `metadata` export, internal `<a>` → `<Link>`.
- Deleted `pages/` entirely (`index.tsx`, `about.tsx`, `_app.tsx`, `_document.tsx`).

**Verification:** `next build` succeeds (Turbopack); `/` and `/about` prerender as static. Runtime curl confirms exact titles (`Home Page` / `About Us`), descriptions, favicon, auto viewport, and nav links render identically to the original.
